subject: Public privacy copy for API console: simplify retention + subprocessors blurb
messages:

Subject: Public privacy copy for API console: simplify retention + subprocessors blurb

Hi Kim / Marissa —

We have a request from Acme Health (security) asking for clearer public language on two things:
1) Hosted API and Console request/response logging retention (they want assurance on min/max retention and how to request deletion).
2) A short, non-legal blurb explaining subprocessors and where the canonical list lives (they asked for a customer-facing sentence we can paste into vendor lists).

I attached a first-pass doc (console_privacy_blurbs_v1.docx) and a subprocessors CSV. Can you advise on customer-facing phrasing that is clear but doesn't expand our legal exposure?

Target: get a single-paragraph snippet for the Console help overlay and one for the public API docs. If needed, I can route to Sales to confirm tone.

Thanks —
Neha
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Product Manager, Privacy & Trust
Redwood Inference

Attachments: console_privacy_blurbs_v1.docx (draft), subprocessors_matrix.csv (export)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Public privacy copy for API console: simplify retention + subprocessors blurb

Thanks Neha — reviewed the draft. High-level comments: we should keep the public-facing snippets short, explicit about what "request/response logs" include, and point to the DPA/Docs for details and deletion requests. Avoid committing to specific retention periods in marketing copy; instead offer ranges and a clear call-to-action to the DPA.

Suggested customer-facing language (short, non-legal):
• "Redwood temporarily retains API request and response logs to ensure reliability, diagnose issues, and improve service performance. Customers can request deletion of their logs through their account team or via our support portal; access to deletion requests is described in our DPA."
• "Redwood maintains a list of subprocessors (third-party service providers) that help us operate and host the service; the current list and subprocessors' roles are published at [link to subprocessors page]."

Redlines in the doc: I swapped out specific day counts for descriptive text (e.g., "short-term" / "as needed for support and security"). If you need to publish an exact retention period, let's sync with infra on exact retention windows per environment.

Also: add a short sentence about transfers — "Where transfers occur, we rely on standard contractual protections and applicable safeguards outlined in our DPA and Data Transfer Addendum." Keep that in the DPA link rather than the overlay.

Happy to finalize wording; let me know if Sales wants softer phrasing for customer-facing pages.

—Kim
Kimberly Park
Lead Counsel, Privacy
Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Public privacy copy for API console: simplify retention + subprocessors blurb

Marissa — can you review Kim's suggested snippets and tell me if this tone works for our customers (particularly regulated ones like Acme)? If yes I'll send the public copy to Acme security for a quick sign-off and then push to the Console help overlay + API docs.

Proposed placement:
- Console: one-line help text on the Settings > Data & Privacy page with a "Learn more" link to the detailed DPA + subprocessors page.
- API docs: small callout on the errors/diagnostics section with the same "Learn more" link.

If Sales needs even softer language, suggest: replace "temporarily retains" with "keeps for a limited time to" — but nothing that implies indefinite retention.

Neha
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Subject: Public privacy copy: request for feedback (Acme Health)

Hi Emma —

Following our call, attached is the short public wording Redwood proposes for the Console overlay and API docs. We've kept it intentionally concise and linked the DPA for details. Please review and let us know if it's acceptable for your vendor inventory / third-party risk checklist.

Proposed snippets (for quick copy/paste into your vendor list):
1) "Redwood temporarily retains API request and response logs to ensure reliability and diagnose issues. Customers can request deletion via their account team or support portal; details are provided in our DPA."
2) "Redwood publishes a canonical list of subprocessors and their roles at: https://redwood.ai/subprocessors (for operational details and contact points)."

Attachments: console_privacy_blurbs_v1.docx (with Kim's redlines)

Thanks —
